defect_families.evidence: Every time in the new code comes from the injected Clock: the ledger claim/dispatch/completion instants, the intake processed_at, and the SmartPromptMachine cutoff. The authorization's own issue_updated_at is caller data and never becomes a cutoff, ordering or admission decision -- test_caller_supplied_issue_time_is_never_execution_authority drives a year-2099 value through a successful execution. The intake boundary's own trusted-cutoff sampling (max of clock and newest durable admission, taken after the write lock) is unchanged and still owns the authority cutoff. Naive datetimes are refused (test_ledger_rejects_naive_times).

The ledger makes no decision across two views: claim does its existence check and its insert inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and both state transitions are single conditional UPDATE statements whose WHERE clause carries the expected prior state and the exact authorization digest, so there is no read-then-write split to drift. The ADR 0036 boundary's single-snapshot authority-plus-write transaction is used unchanged. The compiler resolves authority a second time, later and outside that lock; that resolution can only observe an equal or newer authority head, so a restrictive successor blocks the build rather than being missed -- the drift direction is fail-closed, and the already-durable intake is governed by its own snapshot.

No identity in this path is caller-selected. authorization_id is recomputed from the document's claims and the carried value is only compared, never trusted (test_replay_identity_is_bound_to_exact_authorization_content). document_id comes from the existing content-derived evidence_document_id, execution_owner_id and the intake candidate_id are derived from the recomputed authorization identity, and the recorded label is the repository constant rather than the Issue's own labels. The ledger binds each row to both the identity and a digest of the complete document, so a transition cannot be applied under a different content (test_ledger_transitions_require_the_exact_claimed_content).

The authorization parser requires the exact field set, the exact schema version and the exact governed label, rejects duplicate JSON keys, non-integer or non-positive issue numbers, blank required fields and oversized documents. Configuration is all-or-nothing: each of the eight required variables fails closed on absence, and a malformed verification key fails closed. Absent authority is never read as permission -- an absent authority database, an unpublished document scope and an earlier cutoff all raise rather than substituting current state (test_absent_authority_database_cannot_degrade_to_a_test_double, test_missing_source_handling_authority_for_the_document_fails_closed, test_unknown_document_scope_is_returned_as_absence_not_substituted, test_authority_absent_at_an_earlier_cutoff_is_not_substituted_by_current_state).

The intake reference deliberately carries only the two governed operational metadata fields, and the labels value is the repository constant rather than the Issue's own labels, so no Issue-controlled text can ride into a durable row through the operational-metadata category (test_intake_reference_carries_only_governed_operational_metadata). Issue title and body travel only through their own governed categories, and the resolved FACT persistence restriction and POLICY retention decision block the durable write when they do not permit it (test_fact_persistence_restriction_blocks_durable_intake_and_dispatch, test_denied_retention_blocks_durable_intake_and_dispatch), with no dispatch and no durable document in either case. Downstream, the handoff is non-content lineage only (test_no_issue_text_reaches_the_fallback_runtime).

Ledger state advances only forwards: each transition names its expected prior state, so completion cannot skip the durable dispatch record and a completed authorization can be neither re-dispatched nor re-claimed (test_ledger_state_is_monotonic). Ownership survives a process restart because it is durable rather than in-memory (test_replay_after_process_restart_does_not_execute_again, test_ledger_survives_a_reopened_database), and a crash between the durable handoff record and the dispatch leaves a row that refuses the retry (test_crash_between_handoff_persistence_and_dispatch_cannot_duplicate). Every one of these runs under a frozen clock, so no ordering guarantee depends on the clock advancing.

The authorization binds the exact content it was minted for: its identity is the digest of its own claims, so it cannot be carried onto different Issue content, and the ledger row additionally binds a digest of the complete document. It cannot be replayed onto a different operation either -- the task key, prompt profile and route registry are repository constants, and the execution branch, checkout and destination come from captured configuration, so nothing in the document selects what runs (test_issue_text_cannot_choose_route_provider_destination_or_merge). Downstream the signed envelope remains the only accepted lineage: a tampered handoff is refused by the existing verifier (test_tampered_handoff_fails_the_existing_verifier), and an issuer key swapped after bootstrap cannot produce a dispatchable handoff (test_signing_key_swapped_after_bootstrap_cannot_issue_a_dispatchable_handoff).

This review is the complete single adversarial batch over the exact base->HEAD content of 3a73af22f261fa38611926d3aa996a2aecd724a3..HEAD, covering all eleven required dimensions and every applicable recurring-defect family, recorded before Ready. Both findings below were found by this pass and repaired in the reviewed content.

findings.evidence: The first draft claimed durable ownership before performing the purely local mapping validation, so an authorization that could never execute -- an Issue with an empty body, say -- still permanently consumed its own identity. Repaired by moving the pure mapping and its validation ahead of the claim; nothing durable or external happens before the claim, so the ownership-before-execution ordering is unchanged. Pinned by test_empty_issue_body_fails_closed and test_crash_before_any_execution_still_owns_the_authorization.

The authorization document carries a SHA-256 identity, not a signature, so it is not self-authenticating: anyone able to reach the trusted issuer endpoint can mint a syntactically valid document for content of their choosing. Judged non-blocking rather than ignored: redesigning the PR #391 issuer edge is outside this Issue's authorized scope, and a second independent gate already holds -- the governed document scope is derived from the exact Issue content, so forged content resolves to a scope for which no FACT, POLICY or FIELD_CATEGORY_REGISTRY was ever published and the execution fails closed before a build exists. Pinned by test_a_forged_authorization_still_cannot_execute_arbitrary_content, and the operator's transport-authentication responsibility is now stated explicitly in docs/ISSUE_AGENT_TRIGGER.md rather than left implied.
